title: Embedded Playground: SDK Sandbox Starter Pack
author: Asha Patel
body: ## Summary This page describes the "embedded playground" starter pack for SDK teams who want an in-product, lightweight sandbox runner that can be embedded in developer docs, support consoles, or internal demos. The pack includes: a minimal React frontend, a Node-based backend proxy that enforces rate limits and telemetry, and a recommended deployment pattern for staging and production. Use this when you need a reproducible, observable demo environment that mirrors production API behaviour without exposing raw credentials or unlimited quotas. --- ## Goals - Provide a secure, low-friction way to run SDK code snippets live in docs and support flows. - Ensure parity with production runtime behaviour (timeouts, retries, streaming) for meaningful developer experience. - Bake in telemetry and canonical error handling so support can reproduce customer issues reliably. ## When to use this starter pack - Documentation pages that offer "Try it" interactive examples. - Internal training and onboarding sandboxes for new hires. - Support playbooks where agents need to reproduce a call quickly. - Feature demos that require predictable quotas and no risk of leaking keys. ## What you get in the repo (files & roles) - README.md — setup and maintenance notes. - frontend/ — React app with an embedded code editor and result pane. - backend/ — Node Express proxy, request validation, rate-limiter hooks. - infra/ — Helm chart + k8s manifests for staging and prod. - telemetry/ — pre-configured OpenTelemetry YAML and sample dashboards. - templates/ — HTML snippet and SDK snippet templates for docs. ## Quickstart: Local dev (10–15 minutes) 1. Clone the starter pack: `git clone git@internal:redwood/playground-starter.git` 2. Copy .env.example -> .env and set DEV_API_KEY to a scoped sandbox key (see Access below). 3. Start the backend: ```bash cd backend npm install npm run dev ``` 4. Start the frontend: ```bash cd frontend npm install npm run start ``` 5. Open http://localhost:3000 and paste sample prompts from templates/example-prompts.md Notes: the backend will validate the sandbox key and attach `x-rd-playground=true` header to calls so telemetry and cost accounting are isolated. ## Example: Embedded React snippet (copy into docs) This minimal snippet renders an editor and calls the sandbox endpoint. It is intentionally small and safe for public docs. ```jsx import React, {useState} from 'react' export default function PlaygroundEmbed() { const [prompt, setPrompt] = useState('Write a haiku about engineering') const [out, setOut] = useState('') async function run() { const resp = await fetch('/api/playground/run', { method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify({prompt}) }) const data = await resp.json() setOut(data.result || data.error) } return (
